sections.content:
14,045 people

were counted on the census as "elementary storage occupations (other)" in England and Wales in March 2021.

People who do this type of work may supply berthed ships with water, oil and petroleum, load and unload cargo from ships, boats and barges, and perform other elementary goods handling and storage related tasks not elsewhere classified.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "elementary storage occupations (other)" there were more men than women (80.3% compared with 19.7%).

This means "elementary storage occupations (other)" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "elementary administration and service occupations".

Men made up 80.3% and women made up 19.7% of "elementary storage occupations (other)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "elementary storage occupations (other)" included:

  • managers in storage and warehousing
  • IT operations technicians
  • production managers and directors in mining and energy

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "elementary storage occupations (other)" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "elementary storage occupations (other)", 12.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "elementary storage occupations (other)" was 65 years or older.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "elementary storage occupations (other)" included:

  • aircraft maintenance and related trades
  • vehicle technicians, mechanics and electricians
  • electrical and electronics technicians

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "elementary storage occupations (other)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "elementary storage occupations (other)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "elementary storage occupations (other)", 9.2% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (75.1% compared with 24.9%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (89.2%) than self-employed (10.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the East of England. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included North East Lincolnshire, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
